segmentation.text: walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
to move around such an obstruction.
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and (d) Must return to the sidewalk as soon as practicable.

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate', not expanded.

Walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk: the pedestrian moves (drv.motion.moving, 'in motion ... in any direction') with its footprint on st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (rel.occupies); not a crosswalk.

An obstruction to mobility is st.obstruction 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user' (kinds include sidewalk_fixture, excavation, barrier, debris); encountering it on the sidewalk is the pedestrian, on the sidewalk (rel.occupies st.sidewalk), coming within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of it (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), a reach relating a region to a road user.
Proceeding: the pedestrian moves on (drv.motion.moving) off the sidewalk; it marks the start of the detour.

On the immediately adjacent highway: the pedestrian's footprint overlaps the st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') that the sidewalk it left lies on (st.on_way), and no st.sidewalk.

To move around the obstruction is a purpose read through the conduct it explains: the detour episode, from the pedestrian leaving the sidewalk at an obstruction it encountered (within reach, st.region_geometry) until it is back on a sidewalk.
Such a pedestrian: the same pedestrian aggregate member, on its detour.

Walking or traveling on the highway during the detour (rel.occupies st.highway) as far to the side near the sidewalk: the ground distance from the pedestrian's body to the sidewalk it left (st.region_geometry, st.sidewalk).

A lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters is st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; the pedestrian's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). The words name the lane's purpose, not road users of those classes, so no aggregate is claimed.

operationalizations.standard: as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk as possible
operationalizations.convention: Pedestrian facility design: a detouring pedestrian keeps as close to the sidewalk as possible where its body stays within one pedestrian width plus a shy distance of the sidewalk (st.region_geometry distance).

assumptions.meaning: A short section of the sidewalk on which the pedestrian is travelling is missing or cannot be passed on foot, at the place the pedestrian leaves it.
The area of the highway between the bicycle lane or path the pedestrian occupies and the adjacent sidewalk cannot be passed on foot at the observation.

residues.why: 'With due care' qualifies the permission to leave the sidewalk; the duty to keep to the side applies to such a pedestrian whether or not care was taken, so the words add no restriction to this duty.
Permission (b) concerns the direction of travel on the highway; the duty to keep to the side near the sidewalk is the same in either direction, so the words add no restriction to this duty.

applicability: x is a pedestrian. Judged at each observation of a detour: x's footprint overlaps a highway region h (st.highway) and no sidewalk, and x has been off every sidewalk continuously since an observation at which x was moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) on a sidewalk w lying on h (st.on_way w h), at which either an obstruction o (st.obstruction) was within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry) or asm.sidewalk_section_missing_or_impassable held. Not applicable (exception c) where x's footprint overlaps a bicycle lane or path (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) and asm.area_beside_bicycle_lane_impassable holds.
obligation: x's body is within p.pedestrian_detour_side_distance of the sidewalk w it left (st.region_geometry ground distance from x to w).

narrowings.why: The purpose of moving around the obstruction is read through the detour conduct: off the sidewalk since leaving it at an encountered obstruction.
'As possible' is read as a fixed lateral bound from the sidewalk; an obstruction that itself extends into the highway beyond that bound is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Pedestrian x walks on sidewalk w (on highway h), comes within 1 m of a st.obstruction of kind excavation, steps onto the roadway of h and walks 4 m from w.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but x walks on the roadway 0.4 m from the edge of w.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x walks on the sidewalk throughout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.region_geometry is absent, so neither the encounter nor x's distance to the sidewalk can be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On its detour x walks in a bicycle lane 3 m from w and the trace declares asm.area_beside_bicycle_lane_impassable true.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1, but the trace declares asm.area_beside_bicycle_lane_impassable false.

param_proposals.name: p.obstruction_encounter_reach
param_proposals.convention: Distance between a pedestrian's body and an obstruction within which the pedestrian is at the obstruction (encountering it, or moving around it).
param_proposals.source: Pedestrian lateral clearance and shy distance (AASHTO Guide for the Planning, Design and Operation of Pedestrian Facilities)

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_detour_side_distance
param_proposals.convention: Largest distance between a detouring pedestrian's body and the sidewalk that is still as far to the side near the sidewalk as possible: one pedestrian width plus a shy distance from the curb.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Pedestrian Guide: pedestrian space width (about 0.75 m) plus shy distance

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)
